original_test_intent: Verify that the approved NVMe bay's Access/Busy LED follows the platform-defined idle and active behavior during controlled I/O without unexpected storage errors.
original_method: A qualified operator inserts and watches the exact drive while the agent runs one approved read-only or isolated-file workload against its stable volume, correlating workload timestamps, device counters, LED evidence and complete health/log state.
manual_activity: User approves the LED/workload/data boundary; qualified operator inserts the drive and records idle/active/post-I/O states; agent runs only the approved workload and collects evidence.
required_inputs: Platform Access/Busy state, color, cadence and timing specification
Supported insertion procedure and qualified operator
Read-only or isolated-file workload, rate/duration and data boundary
Backup, RAID/mount recovery, OOB and abort thresholds
safety_requirements: Bind workload to stable drive/volume and exclude boot, production, unknown and raw targets
Verify hot-swap support and data/RAID state before insertion
Preserve logs and record exact workload start/stop
Stop on wrong target, unexpected write, RAID/filesystem/I/O/thermal/power/BMC error or anomalous LED
Do not use Locate or generic control as activity proof
agent_execution_scope: Capture stable idle baseline, I/O counters and physical mapping
Launch/stop the approved tracked workload and collect target-specific telemetry
Collect complete controller/RAID/mount/NVMe/health and OS/BMC logs
Do not insert hardware, observe LED remotely, rebuild/recover or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve LED semantics, exact target/workload/data and recovery
Provide operator and judge physical coverage
Review synchronized I/O/LED/health evidence and decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Locate is an explicit indicator-control function and does not exercise ordinary access/busy behavior; assumed /c0/e/s mapping is unsafe and a CLI response is not visual proof.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Run a bounded approved read-only or isolated-file workload on the stable target with per-device counters and complete health/log capture while the operator records idle, active and return-to-idle LED behavior.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: NVMe insertion, Access/Busy LED check and source 5/5 timing fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a three-phase idle/activity/recovery observation with synchronized target I/O telemetry and physical evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces non-equivalent Locate control with actual safe device activity and auditable timing.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Automation generates and measures activity but never replaces physical LED observation.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Controller caching or background RAID work can blur LED correlation; target counters and a defined quiet interval are required.

project_override_considerations: If the platform combines activity with another indicator or aggregates multiple drives per LED, the vendor state table must define acceptable correlation and target scope.
expected_evidence: Operator identity and timestamped idle/active/post-I/O photos or video
Exact workload target, command, PID, duration, output and counters

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master clearly requires Access/Busy behavior; DeepSeek's Locate method is incomplete/non-equivalent rather than a source ambiguity.

blocked_analysis.analysis: LED definition, safe workload and operator are supplyable prerequisites; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Uses real identity-bound I/O and synchronized telemetry instead of a Locate shortcut, preserving physical observation and data safety.
independent_technical_reasoning: An activity LED is evidence of controller/device traffic, not of a management Locate bit. Because caches and background RAID tasks can generate light without the intended workload, acceptance needs target-specific counters and a controlled transition from quiet to active and back to quiet aligned with the operator's visual record.
